title: Paper Towels 6-roll

adjustment.analysis: No events or price change in target week. The classical uplift model suggests a 21% drop due to the week after a promotion, but the last promotion was on 2026-06-29 (Independence Day), and the week after (2026-07-06) is not immediately following a promotion in the planner notes. The 2026-06-29 promotion was a large one (25% off, holiday, ad feature), but its aftereffect is already reflected in the baseline’s trend. The noise-adjusted uplift effect is x0.79, but it is based on past patterns, not current evidence. No other drivers are active. The baseline already captures seasonal and trend effects. No reason to adjust the median or spread.

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 97.0 | 5%-95%: 56.5 - 219.8 | 10%-90%: 64.1 - 189.6

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-23% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
